incident-bot: PROD ALERT: sudden kv-cache eviction spike + continuous-batching backlog detected in us-west-2. Affected services: streaming-inferer, kv-cache-worker. Severity: P1.
Jordan (oncall): 👀 I'm on it. Seeing elevated paging and token cadence stalls reported by tracing. Full logs coming.
Maya (eng-runtime): I'm pulling the metric dashboards — cache size + eviction rate look like a runaway after the canary that lowered prefetch threshold yesterday.
Ben (eng-sre): Noted. Are customer-facing streams dropping or just slow? Alex, any support tickets?
Alex (support): Two customers reported aborted streams and partial outputs. Both on Dedicated clusters in us-west-2. Ticket IDs: #4521, #4528. Sending them a brief "we're investigating" now. :thumbsup:
Jordan (oncall): Quick mitigation plan: 1) increase eviction throttle to reduce churn 2) revert yesterday's prefetch throttle 3) apply batch-config hotfix to limit continuous-batch window. Can someone push the config change?
Maya (eng-runtime): I can push a staged rollback of prefetch config to canary -> then global. Preparing command.
Maya (eng-runtime): Command to rollback prefetch (run on control-plane):
```
redwoodctl config set kv.prefetch.threshold=0.38 --env=prod --region=us-west-2 --reason="hotfix-rollback-eviction-spike"
```
Jordan (oncall): +1. Ben, can you raise eviction throttle on cache nodes? We want immediate headroom.
Ben (eng-sre): Running eviction throttle bump now (target +40%). Using ops-bot playbook.
ops-bot: Executing playbook: cache/eviction-throttle/increase --region us-west-2 --delta 0.40
ops-bot: Playbook stage 1 complete: nodes drained and throttle updated.
Sophia (eng-ml): Observability note: continuous batching backlog correlates to open KV requests for long sequences. Might be the partial flush bug we've seen before when large KV pages get evicted mid-stream. Recommend enabling conservative partial-flush guard.
Maya (eng-runtime): Adding guard flag now: `runtime.flags.partial_flush_guard=true` on streaming-inferer. Rolling to 10% first.
Maya (eng-runtime): Rollout logs:
```
kubectl -n streaming rollout restart deploy/streaming-inferer
kubectl -n streaming set env deploy/streaming-inferer PARTIAL_FLUSH_GUARD=true
```
Alex (support): Customer update drafted and sent: "We're mitigating an intermittent degradation impacting streaming sessions in us-west-2. Engineers have applied temporary configuration changes. We'll follow up with root cause and ETA"
Jordan (oncall): Monitoring latency and error rates. Initial signal: 60% reduction in aborted streams within 8 minutes after throttle bump and partial-flush guard rollout. Good.
Ben (eng-sre): Eviction rate down from 9k/min to 2.3k/min. Paging IO reduced. Continuous-batch queue length also dropping.
Sophia (eng-ml): Quality check: ensure batch hotfix didn't change token cadence semantics. Running smoke prompts against canary.
Maya (eng-runtime): Smoke test results (canary): streaming tokens delivered at steady cadence, no partial outputs in 200 runs.
Jordan (oncall): Good. Next steps: leave mitigation in place, collect 2h of metrics, prepare incident page, schedule oncall->eng-handoff for full postmortem.
Ben (eng-sre): I've pinned a temporary limit on batch window to avoid amplification: `batch.window.max_ms=250` until a proper tuning jet is in.
Alex (support): Customers informed, one asked about replaying failed sessions — ops will assist.
incident-bot: Incident created INC-2415009999; severity P1; status: mitigating.
Jordan (oncall): Handoff to Maya for follow-up. I'm pausing pager but will stay on slack thread for questions.
Maya (eng-runtime): Taking handoff. I'll coordinate with Sophia for root cause analysis and Ben for infra changes. Target: postmortem draft within 48h.
Sophia (eng-ml): Hypothesis: the lowered prefetch threshold increased cache miss amplification; with continuous batching it's causing many in-flight KV references to race eviction -> partial flush. We'll instrument more detailed KV lifecycle traces.
Maya (eng-runtime): Commands to pull KV traces for window 2415009000-2415012000:
```
redwoodctl logs query --service=kv-cache-worker --since=2415009000 --until=2415012000 --filter="evict OR partial_flush"
```
Ben (eng-sre): I'll keep throttle delta and batch window limit until postmortem. Creating a runbook entry for this scenario.
Alex (support): Updated tickets and customers informed that mitigations are stable for now.
Jordan (oncall): Thanks all. If metrics re-escalate, page me. Otherwise, handoff complete. :white_check_mark:
Maya (eng-runtime): Closing mitigation phase notes here. Will attach logs and timeline to INC-2415009999.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2415009999 status updated: mitigating -> monitoring.
Maya (eng-runtime): Postmortem owners: Maya, Ben, Sophia. Related PRs: runtime#4821 (partial-flush-guard), infra#510 (eviction-throttle-tooling).
Sophia (eng-ml): Also flag for QA: regression test to simulate heavy sequence KV churn and sustained continuous-batching under lowered prefetch.
Jordan (oncall): Final note: customer impact limited to specific Dedicated clusters; no data loss reported, only degraded/aborted streaming sessions. We'll follow up with exact RCAs.
Maya (eng-runtime): End of thread."
